hook: An LLM-assisted proof raises the proven minimum rope length for tying any knot with C crossings.
summary: The shortest rope that can tie a knot of unit thickness has a proven lower bound, and this paper lifts its coefficient from 1.105 to 2.0996 times C^(3/4) for crossing number C. A second bound ties length to stick number, L at least pi(s-1), which tightens bounds for at least 41 torus knots. The author worked with a chatbot and says it failed on many other problems. Only lower bounds improved; upper bounds are unchanged.
title: LLM-Assisted Advances in the Ropelength Problem
